cultural.vision_reason: The image shows a traditional Hawaiian feather helmet base (mahiole) made of ‘ie’ie basketry with a crested form and chevron plaiting patterns, a well-documented Native Hawaiian ceremonial headgear associated with chiefly regalia. This clearly matches the claimed culture and object type.

physical.title: mahiole
physical.summary: Helmet (mahiole) made of basketry made from ‘ie’ie basketry with a wide crest, with a decorative pattern of dark brown plaited into the natural colour of the rootlets. There are three bands of decorative plaiting consisting of parallel chevron/zigzag lines on each side of the cap following the curve of the crest from the narrowest round the ear containers to the widest and boldest near the crest; two similarly bold bands of the same decorative pattern are on each side of the crest, the top of which has six longitudinal dark narrow decorative lines.

cultural.vision_reason: This is a Hawaiian feather "god's eye" (mahiole/akua-related ritual ornament) made with traditional o'o and 'i'iwi feathers and a pearl shell "eye," a well-documented traditional Native Hawaiian ritual object rather than mere jewelry.

physical.title: religious/ritual equipment (?); ornament (?)
physical.summary: Feather god's eye. Disk made of strips of cane (?), slightly concave. The concave side is covered with small bunches of feathers: yellow O'o feathers in a border around the outside edge, red iwi feathers within this, surrounding a central disk of pearl shell (representing the white of an eye), and a patch of black feathers above the pearl shell (representing an eyebrow). The pearl shell disk is pierced and held in place by a wooden peg, with a rounded tip (representing the pupil of an eye). On the back is fixed a plaited band of vegetable fibre, ending in a thin plaited fibre loop.

cultural.vision_reason: The carving shows classic Hawaiian temple image (akua ki‘i) construction — soft wood head with kapa-covered face, pearl-shell eyes, shark's-teeth mouth, and twisted fiber cordage helmet-crest — all hallmark features of Hawaiian ritual sculpture.

physical.title: figure
physical.summary:
Description by C H Read in 1895:
Head probably of an idol carved in very soft wood and represented wearing a low crested helmet. The face is covered with brown kapa [barkcloth], but the nose is covered with a piece of some animal's skin to which some brown fur still adheres. The eyes are formed of pointed oval pieces of pearl-shell perforated in the centre: the left eye has a lump of tapa in the perforation. The open mouth is set irregularly with shark's teeth. The top of the helmet-crest is covered with twisted fibre cord, the strands of which are alternately brown and black. The cap of the helmet is represented by a broad binding of the same cord passing across the temples and down the back of the head. A band consisting of five strings of the same cord runs from the back of the head across the upper lip, and the neck is bound for some distance with the same, the lower part however being bare wood apparently in two pieces, one of which is cylindrical and perforated vertically. The sides of the helmet-crest were originally covered with the patches of the skin of some small animal (rat?) overlaid with dark brown kapa; but on the left side the kapa has entirely disappeared, while on the right side the lower three quarters are intact. The ends of the black and brown cord hang loose from the base of the helmet.

cultural.vision_reason: This is a classic Hawaiian feathered war-god image (akua kaʻai/ʻaumakua type), constructed of wickerwork base with olona-cord netting, red and white feathers, pearl-shell eyes, and dog-teeth mouth — a well-documented Native Hawaiian ritual object form.

physical.title: figure
physical.summary:
Registration slip description by C H Read written in or after 1895:
War-god consisting of a grotesque crested head with elongated neck, made of wicker-work of ie-ie & overlaid with a fine netting of olona-cord covered with red feathers. The top & the sides of the crest are covered with white feathers spotted with occasional red feathers. The eyebrows which rise almost perpendicularly are of black feathers, the eyes being formed of long pointed ovals of pearl-shell with seed pupils. The distended mouth, the corners of which turn sharply upwards, is set with dogs' teeth: the interior is filled with featherwork, the feathers being in alternate red & white bands. The mouth appears to have been originally bordered with a double narrow band of black & yellow feathers. The ears seem to be indicated by small transverse bands of yellow feathers near the crest. The base of the neck also had a border of yellow feathers, only a few of which now remain.
